subject: Human Evolution
title: Mousterian Tools
description: A short lesson to help you apply Mousterian Tools.

hook.text: Neanderthal tools don't look flashy, but look closer—they required dozens of precise steps to produce.

buildup.text: The Levallois technique involves shaping a stone core into a turtle-shell form, then striking one perfect flake.

discovery.text: Each flake is pre-designed: the shape is determined before the final blow. That's planning ahead.

twist.text: Modern knappers say Levallois is harder to learn than many Upper Paleolithic techniques Homo sapiens used.

climax.text: Neanderthal toolmaking proves sophisticated cognition—planning, sequencing, and material understanding.

quiz.question: What is the Levallois technique?
options: A method of pre-shaping a stone core to produce designed flakes
